frontier.hypothesis: One extra IN-LOOP reference to the end pointer (var_t0), with its live range allowed to grow by up to two insns, transposes allocnos 73 and 78 and closes the function.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare seats the eight mutually-conflicting allocnos into [$3,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9,$10,$11] strictly by pri = floor_log2(refs)*refs/live_length. On the floor-5 form pri(78) = 0.888 must land inside (pri(73) = 1.0435, pri(75) = 1.350). In-loop references weigh 2 (flow.c:434 sets depth=1 outside, +1 per NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG; flow.c:2081 etc. add loop_depth per OCCURRENCE), so one extra in-loop raw reference takes refs 4 -> 6, and 12/9 = 1.333, 12/10 = 1.200 and 12/11 = 1.0909 all sit inside the window. reg_n_refs is computed in flow.c BEFORE combine, so an occurrence that combine later folds away still counts toward the priority while costing no instruction.

frontier.hypothesis: If the extra in-loop reference cannot be had without perturbing an instruction, the same swap is reachable from the other side by lowering the counter's priority instead.
frontier.mechanism: pri(73) must drop below pri(78) = 0.888 while staying above pri(74) = 0.750. With refs 7 (floor_log2 = 2) that needs live_length in (15.8, 18.7) against a measured 23; with refs 8 it needs live_length in (27, 32). The counter is live from its init (before the `if`) to the bottom test, so its live range shortens if the init moves inside the guarded body — which costs the blez delay-slot fill and must therefore be paired with another insn that reorg can steal.
frontier.next_probe: Measure the counter's live_length as a function of where `var_t1 = 0;` sits and of the statement order inside the guarded preheader, using tmp/grind/func_80037B00/s7/rainfo.sh, while checking the delay slot in the disassembly each time. Look specifically for a preheader ordering that keeps the blez slot filled by some other insn while shortening the counter's range into 16-18 at refs 7.

frontier.hypothesis: The tie-break route: pseudo numbers follow C declaration order exactly in this function, so an exact priority TIE between the counter and the end pointer closes the swap through declaration order alone.
frontier.mechanism: global.c breaks priority ties in favour of the lower pseudo number, and s7 measured that pseudos are assigned in C declaration order. Declaring var_t0 before var_t1 makes the end pointer the lower-numbered allocno, so any spelling that produces pri(78) == pri(73) exactly seats the end pointer first. With the current numbers that means, e.g., refs(78) = 6 / live 9 = 1.333 against refs(73) = 8 / live 18, or refs(78) = 4 / live 9 = 0.888 against refs(73) = 8 / live 27.
frontier.next_probe: Treat this as the fallback if the refs-6 row is unreachable: it needs a lever on one of the two live lengths anyway. If a structural change ever lands both priorities on the same value, reorder the declarations so var_t0 precedes var_t1 and re-measure — declaration reordering is ordinary C and costs nothing.
